author: John Moore (Firm: New York)
repository: Columbia University Libraries, digitized copy at Internet Archive
locator: Printed p.1 BUGGY HARNESS No.1, direct page image at https://archive.org/download/fineharnesssaddl1891john/page/n2.jpg; printed p.16 English Style Coach Harness at page/n17.jpg; printed p.34 English Saddles illustration at page/n35.jpg. Image endpoint n is the zero-based DjVu object index, not scandata leafNum.
rights_note: Reasoned US public-domain assessment based on New York publication in 1891. Internet Archive metadata supplies publication information but no explicit rights grant. Only factual construction text was used; no plates, image pixels, base meshes or textures were derived.
note: Printedp1 was directly viewed2026-10-22 and confirms No.1 folded/stitched breastcollar, breeching/girth, straight stitched1-inch traces, flat reins, neat bridle, round check rein and platedfront;25.4mm conversion is text-supported. No.1 has no complete harness drawing on that text page; exact strap routes, fittings, buckle/mouthpiece construction and fit remain reconstructed. Printedp16 No.100 describes an English coach family with patentleather collars, platednickel hames and1 1/4-inch traces; this is a separate family, never silently combined with No.1. Printedp34 depicts an English riding saddle; its underside, dimensions, stirrup attachment and full bridle are not shown. These1891 NewYork commercial records support before1904 American market availability only, not Chicago ownership, popularity ranking or1812/1835 eligibility. No source pixels or new geometry are shipped by this source update.
what_it_supplies: Directly inspected1891 printedp1 light-driving harness component recipe and1-inch(25.4mm) trace width.
Directly inspected printedp16 separate English Style Coach Harness family, No.100 collar/hames and1 1/4-inch trace description.
Directly inspected printedp34 English riding-saddle engraving and advertised starting price; qualitative visible form only.
what_it_does_not_supply: Measured fit to the projecthorse/vehicle, load/pressure suitability or full strap construction.
No.1 complete drawn harness; saddle underside/tree/stirrup geometry; photographic materials or originalcolors.
